name: Azariah
bio:
Azariah (also called Uzziah), son of Amaziah, was made king of Judah at sixteen by the people of Judah after his father was assassinated at Lachish. He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah (2 Kings 14:21-22).

## 📖 Core Story: Fifty-Two Years, and a Lifelong Leprosy

Azariah reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem, doing right in the LORD's eyes as his father Amaziah had, though the high places remained (2 Kings 15:1-7).

Chronicles tells how this reign unfolded and how the leprosy came about. As long as Azariah sought God, under the guidance of a man named Zechariah who understood the visions of God, the LORD gave him success: he defeated the Philistines and tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, received tribute from the Ammonites, built towers and dug wells for his herds and farms, and raised an army of over 307,000 men equipped with shields, spears, and newly invented siege engines for shooting arrows and great stones from the city towers — his fame spread far and wide. But once he grew powerful, his pride led to his downfall: he entered the temple himself to burn incense on the altar, a priestly duty not his to perform. The priest Azariah and eighty other priests confronted him, warning that this would bring him no honor from the LORD, and as Uzziah raged at them, leprosy broke out on his forehead on the spot; the priests hurried him out of the temple, and he lived in a separate house as a leper for the rest of his life while Jotham governed as regent. Isaiah son of Amoz recorded the rest of his reign (2 Chronicles 26:1-23). Azariah was buried with his ancestors in the City of David — in a separate burial field because of his leprosy — and Jotham succeeded him.
